JusPrin 2 is a major upgrade. We rebuilt nearly everything: it is now built on OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and every project has AI working beside it. The goal is the one JusPrin started with: make 3D printing simpler for hobbyists. You tell AI what you are printing and what went wrong. AI reads your file, your settings and your slice, changes the settings and slices again.

## What AI can do

Each project has an AI chat beside the 3D view. Ask in plain words, and AI works in the open project:

- Set up the printer, filament and print settings for the part you are printing.
- Open a model or project file, place objects on the plate, and lay out plates.
- Cut, split, merge and repair objects.
- Change print settings for you.
- Slice the plate and check the result, for example support printed inside a hole, or a part that starts in the air.
- Look at a photo of a failed print and suggest what to change.
- Run a filament calibration test (temperature, flow or pressure advance), read a photo of the printed test, and save the result as a new filament preset.

When you ask AI to print, it opens the usual send dialog. You choose the options and press Send. AI never starts a print.

When a slice has a problem, a marker on the 3D view shows it. Press Ask AI to have AI explain the problem and your options.

## Ways to use AI

- Sign up for a JusPrin account in the app. New accounts get free credits, and no card is needed.
- Use your own OpenAI, Anthropic or OpenRouter API key.
- Connect an AI app you already use: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cowork, Cursor or VS Code. It can then work with the project open in JusPrin.
- Or skip AI and just slice.

## Also new

- **Home screen.** Your projects and printers are on one screen. Each printer card shows the printer's status, and once the printer is connected, opens its own window.
- **Printers.** Add a printer and connect it by chatting with AI. You can connect Bambu Lab printers in LAN mode, and Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint printers.
- **Saving.** Projects save themselves, so JusPrin never asks you to save or discard. File › Save (Cmd+S on a Mac, Ctrl+S on Windows and Linux) keeps a version you can go back to in File › Version history. Saving doesn't write over the .3mf file you opened. To get a .3mf file, use File › Export › Project 3MF (Cmd+Shift+S or Ctrl+Shift+S).
- **Opening files.** A file you open from Finder or File Explorer opens as a new project. A model dropped on the 3D view is added to the open project.
- **Check print.** Print › Check print shows a report of the slice beside the preview.
- **Print history.** Every sliced file you export or send to a printer is listed on Home's Print history, and you can print it again from there.
- **Classic view.** View › Switch to classic view shows OrcaSlicer's full interface. Press Back to JusPrin to return.
- **Updates.** JusPrin checks its GitHub releases for a new version once a day. You see the result in Preferences › Updates.
- **Reporting a problem.** Help › Report a problem opens a new GitHub issue in your browser, with the app's version and your system filled in.

## Upgrading from JusPrin 1.4

- **Installing.** On Windows, the installer replaces JusPrin 1. On a Mac, JusPrin 2 is also called JusPrin.app, so dragging it to Applications replaces JusPrin 1. On Linux, the AppImage is a new file, and JusPrin 1's AppImage stays where it is.
- **Your printers.** The first time JusPrin 2 starts, it offers to import your printers from JusPrin 1 or OrcaSlicer, with their filaments and print settings. You choose which printers to import. You can import later with Printer › Import printers from JusPrin 1 or Import printers from OrcaSlicer.
- **Your JusPrin 1 folder.** JusPrin 2 keeps its settings in a new folder. It only reads JusPrin 1's folder and never changes it. JusPrin 1's app settings, such as units and language, aren't imported.
- **Your account.** Your JusPrin 1 sign-in doesn't carry over. To use AI with a JusPrin account, sign up in JusPrin 2, even if you had an account in JusPrin 1. Chats from JusPrin 1 aren't imported.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.

13:## Before a release
14-
15-The guide is brought in line with the app before each release, on a computer with the app built.
16-
17-1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit to release: the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets.
18-2. Leave the computer alone and run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. It takes about a minute a page, plus the questions.
19-3. Fix what it reports, then run it again until it passes:
20-   - **A label is on no screen.** The app's wording changed. Find the new wording in the app and correct the page.
21-   - **A run failed.** Open its log, which the command names. Either the screen no longer works as the page says, and the page needs correcting, or the harness expects something the app no longer does, and the harness needs correcting.
22-   - **A picture is blank.** The program that started the command may not record the screen. Grant it Screen Recording in the system's privacy settings and run again.
23-   - **AI answered a question wrongly.** Read its reply in the output. Usually the page is unclear or its first line does not say when to read it.
24-4. Look through what changed on screen since the last release (`git log <last release tag>..HEAD -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin`). The command finds what a page gets wrong. It cannot find a new screen or menu item that no page mentions, so add those by hand.
25-5. Commit the pages together with their pictures, the skills the command rebuilt, and `checked-version.txt`. When every step passes for every page, the command writes the app's version to that file. A run with `--skip-app`, with `--area`, or without `--ask-ai` leaves it as it was. The release workflow refuses a version this file does not name. The file says the check passed for that version, not on which commit, so run it on the commit you mean to release.
26-
27-## What the command does
28-
29-1. **Walks the app and takes the pictures.** `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` names, for each page, the runs of the app's test harness that go through the screens the page describes, and the checks in each run the page depends on. `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py` runs them in the app as built and copies the pictures a page uses into `pictures/<page>/`.
30-2. **Rebuilds the copy AI reads.** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds a skill from each page.
31-3. **Checks each page**, in `guide.test.ts` beside it: every label in bold is in the app's source, every section has a run in step 1, every picture is one step 1 took, and the page has questions for step 4. `components/Guide.test.tsx` checks that the app's guide window lists every page and shows each with all its pictures and without the parts written for AI.
32-4. **Asks AI the page's questions** (`--ask-ai`). `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` holds them with what a right answer says. `tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py` asks the model and has a judge read the replies.
33-
34-## Writing a page
35-
36-- Start it with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`: one line, at most 300 bytes, saying when AI should read it. The model reads every page's description together in one list, and the Claude command-line tool that `--ask-ai` runs through cuts a tool description longer than about 2,000 characters, so keep each one short: about 200 bytes. Write `...` rather than `…` in it, since that tool rewrites the one as the other.
37-- Put words that are only for AI in `<!-- ai: … -->`. They are hidden on this site.
38-- Use bold only for words that are on screen, exactly as they are on screen.
39-- A picture goes on a line of its own, as `![what it shows](pictures/<page>/<name>.png)`, and comes from a run named in `guide_checks.json`. AI's copy leaves it out.
40-- A picture is kept at twice the screen's size, and the guide window shows it at half, the size it has on screen. Mark a run's picture that the harness draws at the screen's own size with `"atScreenSize": true`, and the command doubles it.
41-- List a new page at the top of this file, or the guide window leaves it out.
42-- Give each `##` section a run in `guide_checks.json`.
43-- Add at least three questions for the page to `guide_questions.json`.
44-- AI's copy may hold at most 16 KiB. Split a page that grows past that.

=== 3c134d39e3 Report every failure a person cannot act on; keep a sentence only where they can
An error is expected only when the person can do something about it and
Kenneth decided what they are told. Every other failure now stops the work,
travels up unchanged and is reported once, by the handler at the top of its
entry point, and the person reads "Something went wrong on our side".
Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing
about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to
report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as
much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause
analysis. And that's it, nothing else."

Top handlers
- reported(doing, body), in Support/ErrorReport.hpp, wraps every CallAfter
  body, timer, HTTP callback and thread JusPrin's own code starts. Before,
  an exception from a CallAfter or a timer ended the main loop, and one from
  an HTTP callback or a thread called std::terminate: a model list entry
  without "id" aborted the app at launch (exit 134).
- report_unexpected_error moves itself to the main thread when called from
  another. A failure the person already answered in this run is not asked
  about again, so its dialog cannot reopen itself; automatic reports, which
  open no dialog, still send each one.
- An exception leaving any other native event stays OrcaSlicer's, as
  Kenneth decided; GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop is unchanged.

AI requests
- A failed request names its cause only where the person can act. On a
  JusPrin account, by the gateway's error code: signed out, out of credits,
  app too old, request too large, too many requests. With their own key, by
  the HTTP status alone: 401, 413, 429. No answer at all says the service
  could not be reached.
- Every other answer, an error the service sends inside a reply, and a reply
  cut short or unreadable throw UnexpectedServiceAnswer with the service's
  status, request id and body. The sentences for an overloaded, unavailable,
  timed-out, paused or cut-short service are deleted, and
  StreamEvent::Kind::Incomplete with them. The model declining to answer
  (stop reason "refusal") keeps its sentence: it is the model's answer, not
  a failure.
- A tool call that fails in the app's own work still goes to the AI model,
  and is also reported when automatic reports are on, with no dialog. A file
  the person picked that OrcaSlicer will not read answers "refused" and is
  not reported. When the saved projects cannot be read, the call's message
  carries the file system's reason.
- An AI service set up in another window during a reply is installed once
  the reply ends, instead of being dropped.

Account, sign-in and settings
- An account, account box, model list or sign-in answer that is the
  server's fault (a 5xx, or an answer the app cannot read) is reported. No
  answer and a 4xx refusal keep their sentences.
- A key or a sign-in the settings file could not keep throws. The "works
  until restart" warning and its row are gone.
- Delete account waits while a printer or filament chat replies, as it
  already did for the project chat.
- "Sign in" runs the web view's own address check, as "Sign up free" does.
  An address that check passes and the server refuses now reads
  "“alex@gmail” is not a complete email address. Check it, then try again."
  with the address the person typed. The password path is unchanged.

Chats, attachments and saves
- A chat checkpoint, chat switch, restoration or new chat whose save fails
  throws the autosave's own error instead of a sentence made up for it.
  Attachment blobs, attachment folders, the chat-titles file and a stored
  chat state that cannot be read or written throw with the file system's
  error. The timer's own checkpoint leaves alone the one failure the
  autosave has just recorded and already shows as "Couldn't save".
- A message or action a newer build wrote is kept as written and not shown,
  instead of being read as another kind.
- A file dropped on Home is copied with write_file (Support/Files: write,
  then rename), so a write the file system cuts short is an error and not a
  shorter file.

Home and Print history
- A print report answer nobody decided is reported. A refused report shows
  the next step: an ended sign-in shows the chat's sentence for it, an
  unreadable photo "That photo could not be read."
- A photo over 20 MB is refused when it is chosen: "That photo is larger
  than 20 MB. Choose a smaller photo, then send the report again."
- While the projects folder cannot be read, Print history shows Home's
  sentence, "Your projects couldn't be loaded. JusPrin will keep trying.",
  keeps no history, and lists again by itself once the folder can be read.
- An exported G-code file is "not found" only when its path is not there;
  any other failure to read it is reported.
- A printer window whose secure connection cannot be checked says "The
  printer at %s answered, but JusPrin couldn't check its secure connection.
  If the printer's address starts with https://, change it to http:// in
  Printer settings, then try again." Checked on macOS only: on Windows and
  Linux an https address on a printer that only speaks http probably still
  says "Nothing answered".

Start report
- When the server answers the app's start report with a fault, the app
  reports it through report_if_automatic: sent only when automatic reports
  are on, and no dialog opens. When nothing answers (no network, a refused
  connection, a timeout) nothing is reported. Before, both cases only wrote
  a log line. report_if_automatic now moves itself to the main thread, as
  report_unexpected_error does. Kenneth, 2026-11-16, quoting the proposal
  back: "My proposal, not built: no dialog, and a report only when the
  server answers with a fault and the person has automatic reports on.
  Having no network at start stays silent. - go with your proposal".

Kenneth accepted the three new sentences (photo too large, incomplete
address, secure connection) on 2026-11-16: "Yes, all three". They and "That
photo could not be read." are in the catalogs, AI translated in all 22
languages.

Shell harness: new modes --delete-account-waits and --printer-window; the
dialog closer answers only the innermost modal dialog; the stand-in server
answers the account box with 204, as the server does; checks count the app
log's "Unexpected error while" lines where a folder cannot be read or
written; print_history_stopped_print_has_no_row replaces a check that
expected a "Started" row removed on 2026-11-08; the detach check installs an
agent the profile does not pick with --fake-printer too.

=== fbf378bc94 Shell harness: open the printer chat through the shell, as the app does
Several shell harness modes (--printer-setup, --printer-chat-sheet,
--print-host-check, --printer-network-check, --printer-connect-skill)
called PrinterPanel::open directly. That shows the panel but skips the
shell, which in the app hides Home and the project tabs and gives the
chat the whole window. So the harness window showed Home squeezed into
the left half with the chat beside it, a layout no person ever sees.
The real app was checked by opening the printer chat three ways; each
time the chat covered the whole window.

A new helper, open_printer_chat, opens the chat through
ShellController::open_printer_conversation, the path Home and the header
use. The shell opens no chat while one is open, so the helper first
closes an open chat and waits until its close (which finishes on a later
event turn) is done. It then checks that the chat is shown and that Home
is hidden.

Tested on macOS:
- --printer-setup: 348 checks pass, 0 fail. With the old direct opening
  put back, 6 of the new "chat covers Home" checks fail.
- --print-host-check and --printer-chat-sheet: pass.
- --printer-connect-skill: the new checks pass; 3 other checks
  (skill_add_settled, connect_skill_printer_added,
  connect_skill_comes_with_printer_add) fail, the same 3 that fail on
  the unchanged harness.
- --printer-network-check: not run, it needs Bambu's real plug-in.

=== 70f08918d8 Fix two agent tests that failed only on Windows
Two cases in agent_bridge_tests failed on Windows and passed on macOS.
Both mistakes were in the tests; the app code they check was right.

"pick_attachment opens the dialog for one kind and stages the chosen
files" wrote its sample G-code file in text mode. On Windows text mode
writes "\n" as "\r\n", so the app's preview of the file was "G1 X0\r\n"
and the check for "G1 X0\n" failed. The test now writes the file in
binary mode.

"the account comes with the titles of the chats it charged" kept its own
std::ifstream on chat-titles.json open until the end of the test, and the
last line deletes the temp folder. Windows refuses to delete an open
file, so remove_all threw. The test now closes the file as soon as it
has parsed it.

Tested: agent_bridge_tests passes in full on Windows (579 cases, on the
GCP test VM) and on macOS (581 cases), and each of the two cases passes
when run alone on Windows.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7KJ0NZFQ5B5SEAB588M9FJZ

=== f88b40865c Connect every print host type from the printer chat, not only Moonraker and OctoPrint
GitHub issue TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#40: an Elegoo Centauri Carbon
could not be connected from its printer chat. Its profile saves it with the
Elegoo Link connection type, and the chat refused every type except
Moonraker and OctoPrint. The AI asked to connect it as Moonraker, and the
app refused before sending any request to the printer.
Nothing in the history or earlier sessions gave a reason for the limit.
Kenneth, asked whether to open it to Elegoo Link only or to every type: "To every type."

printer_host_connect now takes every connection type OrcaSlicer's printer
settings offer except the three online services the person signs in to
(Obico, SimplyPrint, 3DPrinterOS), which need that sign-in, not an address.
Moonraker and OctoPrint keep their own tests. Every other type runs
OrcaSlicer's own test for it, the one its Physical Printer dialog's Test
button runs, unchanged. Those requests have no time limit, so the test runs
on a thread of its own and the chat gives up after the same 30 seconds as
the other tests; the thread is left to finish, and against a host that
never answers it holds one socket until the app quits. A refused test
(HTTP 401 or 403) opens the API key form, as it does for Moonraker and
OctoPrint.

A printer with no saved address is no longer reported as "unavailable" for
the type its profile defaults to, since the person never chose that type:
a Neptune 4 or Creality K1 can be connected as Moonraker. The connection
skill now says the saved type is the starting point, explains Elegoo Link
model by model from the app's code (Centauri Carbon: its web page names
ELEGOO, no key; Centauri Carbon 2: an access code, 123456 by default, typed
in the form labelled "API key"), and names the types the chat cannot finish
(Repetier, UltiMaker, PrusaLink with a user name and password) and where
the person can. The issue report's footer names the type tried and, when
different, the type the printer is saved with. The guide's sentence on

=== d010a88c1a Read printer sizes the same in every language
When JusPrin runs in a language that writes decimals with a comma
(Portuguese, German, French, Spanish, Russian and others), the add-printer
form showed no nozzle sizes for almost every printer, so the printer could
not be added. GitHub issue TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#39 reports it for
the Flashforge Creator 5 Pro and its 0.4 mm nozzle.

wxWidgets sets the C library's number format to the app's language at
startup. JusPrin's printer catalog read the sizes in the printer profiles
with std::stod, which follows that format, so "0.4" read as 0. With the
number format set to Portuguese, 412 of 454 printer models lost their
nozzle sizes, and fractional bed sizes were cut short (233.5 mm read as
233). The same mistake read a 0.4 mm nozzle in an opened 3MF as 0, and
told the AI about a nozzle mismatch as "0,2" instead of "0.2".

On macOS the bug is usually hidden: an app opened from Finder has no LANG
setting, and the bundled Python's startup then resets the whole C locale
to "C". Python does this only on Unix, so Windows always shows the bug.

The catalog, the printer backend and the 3MF facts now parse with
OrcaSlicer's locale-independent string_to_double_decimal_point and
atof_decimal_point. The mismatch text is written by the JSON library
instead of snprintf. The test programs compile LocalesUtils.cpp directly,
as they do the JusPrin sources they test.

Tested: three new tests switch the number format to Portuguese; each fails
without this change and passes with it. jusprin_tests (180 cases) and
agent_bridge_tests (581 cases) pass, and the clang-tidy include check
passes on the changed lines. In the real app on macOS, started with LANG
set and the language set to Portuguese, JusPrin 2.0.0 showed no nozzle
size for the Creator 5 Pro and kept Continue disabled; this build showed
0.25, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 mm and added the printer with its 0.4 mm profile.
Not run on Windows.

=== b3eed3bf4b Report unexpected errors to the JusPrin team, and fix four bugs found on the way
When something fails that no person can act on, JusPrin now shows one
dialog, "Something went wrong on our side" (boards agent-ui-11 to 16),
instead of a sentence about that particular failure. The person can see
the whole report, press "Report to JusPrin team", or tick "From now on,
report errors like this automatically". The report goes to JusPrin's
server (/ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports), which passes it to Sentry.

Why: under the error-handling rules, a failure with no outcome a person
decided travels up unchanged to the top of its entry point and is
reported there, instead of each site writing its own sentence. Kenneth
agreed to this on 2026-11-15: "Yes, go with this approach."

The reporting path
- Support/ErrorReport: report_unexpected_error() logs the error, then
  sends it at once when automatic reports are on, or queues it for the
  dialog after the current event. A failure that repeats while its dialog
  waits is queued once; after the person answers, the next occurrence
  opens the dialog again, and every occurrence is sent when reports are
  automatic (Kenneth: "leave it"). A report holds the app and OS versions,
  what the app was doing, the error and, for page errors, the stack. The
  home folder becomes "~", a file-system error's paths become "<path>",
  and each field is cut to the server's limit. The send is anonymous: no
  token or cookie.
- Shell/ErrorReportDialog: the dialog, drawn with the design tokens. Its
  line "no chat messages, no files, no project names and no account or
  email address" stays although other error text can quote a file name
  (Kenneth: "Keep the promise and accept the risk.").
- Top handlers: the AI pages' and Home's message handlers, the file
  picker's callback (it reads the chosen files after the page's message
  was handled), and both pages' own top level (window "error" and
  "unhandledrejection", sent as a new report_error message and queued
  until the page has connected).
- An exception that leaves any other native event is handled exactly as
  OrcaSlicer handles it; no OrcaSlicer-owned file is changed. Kenneth: "it
  should behave the same as the upstream. no reason to use a diff
  behavior here for the fork".
- Preferences › Updates: a new "Error reports" box, "Report errors to the
  JusPrin team automatically", off by default.

Five failures now take that path, with their sentences removed:
- "JusPrin couldn't start signing in. Try again." (the AI page and Home)
- "The file could not be read." (an attachment that is not base64, or a
  chosen or dropped file that cannot be opened or read)
- "The G-code couldn't be written to %s." (exporting from print history)
=== 00953649de Translate JusPrin into upstream OrcaSlicer's 22 languages
JusPrin's own windows and its AI and Home pages showed English in every
language. Every string a person reads in them is now marked and translated
into the 22 languages upstream ships, in catalogs of the fork's own so that
taking an upstream release never conflicts in one:

- Localization/native/<lang>.po for native text, collected by
  Localization/update_catalogs.py (text upstream's template already has
  keeps upstream's translation) and merged by Brand/brand_catalogs.py into
  the catalog the app loads.
- Localization/pages/<lang>.po for both pages, through Lingui 5.9.5. The app
  passes its language as ?lang=; the page activates it before any module
  runs.

Text the model reads (prompts, skills, tool results), logs, error reports,
identifiers and names stay English. The translations are machine-made and
marked "# AI Translated"; entries a translator was unsure of also carry
"# Needs human review: <what to check>". Terms follow upstream's catalog
and the OrcaSlicer localization glossary.

Sentences that were built from translated pieces are now one message each,
with placeholders and plural forms, and render the same English. Other
changes the translation needed:

- Support/Translate.hpp: GUI-free code marks text with L() and translates it
  with translated() and translated_plural(), which the app installs.
- "Model" and "Search models" in the printer picker, and "Plate" in the
  add-printer form, have contexts of their own, apart from the AI model and
  the project plate.
- Numbers JusPrin shows use the app language's separators
  (Support/DecimalText on the native side, decimalText on the pages): a
  German app reads "Kobra 3 · 0,4 mm".
- An untitled chat is titled with the translated "New chat"; the saved
  document keeps its English default.
- "Ask current chat about this" drafts its message in the app's language.
- The setup card's estimate row wraps its link to the next line when a
  translation is too long to share the row.
- All settings shows OrcaSlicer's setting labels, groups and values through
  OrcaSlicer's own catalog.
- Translator notes sit on the line of the string they describe, so xgettext
  gives each note to the right string.
- update_catalogs.py starts a new language with its own number of plural
  forms; Home type-checks Lingui from its own packages.

Server text the app shows follows the app's language: the account, account
=== 1c1007fe3b Error handling rules: a sentence of its own only where the person can act
Replaces the "Error handling discipline" list in AGENTS.md.

An error is expected only when the person can do something about it and
Kenneth decided what the product tells them. Every other error is
unexpected: no code where it happens, it travels up unchanged, and the one
handler at the top of the entry point reports it with everything known and
tells the person "Something went wrong on our side".

Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing
about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to
report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as
much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause
analysis. And that's it, nothing else."

The rules name the error-handling skill, which is not in this commit.

input.content:
JusPrin 2.0.1 speaks your language, connects more printers, and fixes adding a printer when the app is set to a language that writes decimals with a comma.

## New

- **Your language.** JusPrin's own windows, Home and the AI chat now follow the app's language, in the 22 languages OrcaSlicer ships. The translations are machine-made; if a sentence reads wrong, tell us with Help › Report a problem. AI still reads and writes in whatever language you chat in.
- **More printers connect from the printer chat.** Besides Bambu Lab, Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint, the chat now connects the other print hosts OrcaSlicer's printer settings offer, such as PrusaLink and Elegoo Link (Elegoo Centauri Carbon and Centauri Carbon 2).
- **Error reports.** When something goes wrong that you can't fix yourself, JusPrin says so in one window and lets you send us a report with one click. You can read the whole report before sending it. It holds no chat messages, files, project names, account or email address. To send these reports without being asked, tick **Report errors to the JusPrin team automatically** in Preferences › Updates.

## Fixed

- In Portuguese, German, French, Spanish, Russian and other languages that write decimals with a comma, the add-printer form showed no nozzle sizes for most printers, so the printer couldn't be added. Bed sizes such as 233.5 mm were also read short.
- A photo larger than 20 MB for a print report is now refused when you choose it, instead of failing when the report is sent.

## Also changed

- Each time JusPrin starts, it tells our server that it started, so we can count how many installs run. The message holds the app's version, the system's name and a random install number made on the first start. It holds nothing that names you. JusPrin doesn't send it when stealth mode is on.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.

Yes, I think we should. I'd put the steps that can be checked into the release workflow, and the rest into a skill (a checklist file in `.claude/skills/` that an agent follows when asked to release). First, I need to correct one thing I told you earlier.

**Correction.** I said the last five commits had never been built on Windows or Linux. That's true today, but the release workflow builds all three platforms itself, through `jusprin_build_all.yml`. If the code didn't compile there, the draft would fail. What the release workflow skips is the test suites. The only test it runs checks its own version logic.

**Steps for every release (my proposal)**

Before starting the workflow:
1. **Tests pass on all three platforms.** That means `agent_bridge_tests`, `jusprin_tests` and the AgentUI page tests on the release commit. Neither the release workflow nor the nightly runs them.
2. **The server is ready for the new app.** Every server address the release calls should answer in production. This is the step 2.0.1 would have missed.
3. **Version and release notes.** The workflow already refuses a release without them. The notes still need your read.
4. **Guide check.** The workflow already refuses a release without it, unless the skip box is ticked.
5. **Live AI checks, only if prompts, skills or tools changed.** These cost money, so they need your OK each time.

Releasing:
6. Push to `jusprin-dev`, fast-forward `main`, and start the workflow with Mac signing on.
7. **Test the draft's own files on Windows, Mac and Linux.** Install over the previous version and start the app. Sign in, have one chat, slice, and check one change listed in the notes on the platform where it matters most.
8. You publish.

After publishing:
9. Reply to and close the issues the release fixes. Update the Homebrew cask.
10. A day later, run the `jusprin-production-check` skill in tsd-enterprise for new failures.

**Why not a skill alone.** A skill only works when an agent loads it and follows it. 2.0.0's steps lived in chat sessions and one memory note, and nobody wrote them down. A check inside the workflow can't be forgotten: the workflow simply refuses the commit. Steps 1 and 2 can be made checks like that. Steps 7 to 10 need a person or judgment, so they belong in the skill.

Decision needed: how should we enforce the release steps? There are three options:
- **A skill only.** About an hour of work. Nothing stops a release that skips a step.
- **A skill, plus two new workflow checks.** One check runs the test suites on all three platforms. That adds about 30–60 minutes of runner time per release. The other posts to every server address the app calls and refuses the release on a 404. This costs half a day to a day of work, and `jusprin_release.yml` gets longer.
- **Workflow checks only, with no skill.** This leaves the draft testing and the after-publish steps written nowhere.

I'd pick the skill plus the two workflow checks. Do you want that?
how about l18n translation? also Check to see if there's a guide on how error handling should be performed and if so, it's probably a good idea to use that before each release.

JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for

catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own

## Updating the catalogs

After marking or changing text:

python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py

content.text:
Yes, both belong on the list before every release. Translations have tools in the repo but nothing runs them automatically. Error handling has a written rule section and a skill that checks a range of commits against it. Neither has been run for this release yet.

**Translations**

The tools are a script and a test:
- `Localization/update_catalogs.py` collects every marked string from the app and the two web pages into the translation files for all 22 languages.
- `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` fails if any entry is untranslated or a translation lost a placeholder.

The weak spot is that nothing runs them for you. If someone adds a sentence and forgets the script, the test never sees that sentence. Also, no workflow on GitHub runs the page tests.

I ran both on the 2.0.1 code just now:
- **The test passes.** Every entry in every language is translated, including the new sentences added on 2026-11-16 (photo over 20 MB, "Something went wrong on our side", the printer secure-connection sentence).
- **The committed translation files were out of date.** They still listed about 30 sentences that the error-handling commit deleted, in all 22 languages. Users wouldn't see this, but it's wrong. Re-running the script moves them to the obsolete section. That change sits in the release worktree, not committed yet, and should go in with the version change.
- **Many translations are flagged unsure.** 422 entries across the languages carry a "Needs human review" note. With about 1,400 entries per language, that's roughly 1 in 70 flagged. All the translations are machine-made.

For the checklist I'd add two things:
- Run the script before the release and fail if it changes any file. Then run the catalog test. Both are mechanical, so they could be checks in the release workflow.

---
name: jusprin-release
description: Use when asked to make, prepare or start a new JusPrin release (a new version on GitHub), from choosing the commit range to the after-publish steps. Covers the version, release notes, server readiness, translations, the error-handling audit, tests, the guide check, moving main, the release workflow, testing the draft and what follows publishing. Not for JusPrin 1 (jusprin-v1) or OrcaSlicer's own releases.
---

# Making a JusPrin release

The release workflow, `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml`, builds the
release files from one commit and uploads them to a draft release on GitHub.
It refuses the commit without a new version, release notes and a guide check
(see "Releasing" in `AGENTS.md`). It does not run the test suites, check the
server, check the translations or audit error handling. This skill covers
those too, in the order they have to happen.

## Kenneth decides these

Ask Kenneth, in plain words, and wait for his yes before each of these. A yes
covers that one action, not the next one.

- The version number, when he has not named it.
- The release notes' wording. Show him the file.
- Deploying the server.
- Spending API money on live AI checks. Say the cost.
- Pushing to `jusprin-dev`, and moving `main` forward.
- Starting the release workflow.
- Downloading the draft's files to this computer.
- Posting anything on GitHub, such as replies to issues.

**Never publish the draft.** Kenneth publishes it by hand on the Releases page.
Never force-push `main`.

## 1. Set up

1. Find the last release: `git tag --list 'jusprin/v*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1`.
   The range is that tag to `origin/jusprin-dev` (after `git fetch origin`).
2. Make your own worktree from `origin/jusprin-dev`, under
   `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`, on a branch named `claude/release-<version>`.
   Never name it `jusprin-release/...`: pushing a branch with that name starts
   an unsigned release build.
3. Read every commit in the range: `git log --format='%h %s%n%b' <range>`.
   Note what a person would notice, and the GitHub issues each change fixes.

## 2. Version and release notes

1. Set `kVersion` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`. It must be
   above every released JusPrin version.
2. Write `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`. The app
   shows this file under "What's new", and the draft starts with it. Follow the
   shape of the previous release's file. Write for a person who prints, not for
   a developer. Check every on-screen label you quote against the source
   (`git grep`), and leave out anything you have not checked.
3. A change that sends anything new from the person's computer, such as a new
   message to our server, goes in the notes and says what it holds.

## 3. Server readiness

The app calls JusPrin's server at `https://jusprinv2.obico.io`. Every address
the release calls must already be deployed there.

```bash
git grep -h -o '"/ent/jusprin/v2/[a-z_/]*' -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin ':!*test*' | tr -d '"' | sort -u
```

GET each one: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://jusprinv2.obico.io<path>`.
Any answer but 404 (200, 401, 403, 405) means the address is there. A 404
means it is not deployed. Find the server change in the tsd-enterprise
repository (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py` on `master`), tell Kenneth what is
missing, and wait until it is deployed. Also tell him about any other server
behavior a change in the range relies on, such as a new error code.

## 4. Translations

1. Run `python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py`. It
   needs GNU gettext and `npm ci` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`. If it
   changes any catalog, those changes go into the release commit.
2. Translate every new entry in every language, following "Localization &
   translations" in `AGENTS.md` and the `orca-translations` skill.
3. `npx vitest run src/catalogs.test.ts` in `AgentUI` must pass: it fails
   while an entry is untranslated or a translation lost a placeholder.
4. Count the entries marked `# Needs human review` in
   `Localization/native/*.po` and `Localization/pages/*.po`. Tell Kenneth the
   count, so he can decide whether someone should read a language.

These steps cannot find a sentence nobody marked for translation. While
reading the range, look for text a person reads that is not marked.

## 5. Error-handling audit

Run the `error-handling` skill on the range. When the release relies on
server changes, audit the tsd-enterprise range too. Report the findings to
Kenneth. A fix lands on `jusprin-dev` as its own commit, and the steps above
are then repeated for the new range.

## 6. Tests

Build in your worktree, in Release, following "Building on a shared machine"
in `AGENTS.md`: check the load first, use `-j4`, choose every target before
you start. Configure with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON`.

- macOS: build `agent_bridge_tests`, `jusprin_tests`, `shell_integration_harness`,
  `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs`, then run both test programs and
  `npm test` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI`.
- Windows and Linux: the release workflow compiles them but runs no tests.
  Run `agent_bridge_tests` and `jusprin_tests` on each. Kenneth keeps test
  machines for both; ask him for access if you do not have it, and say in
  your report if they were not run.
- When the range changes text the model reads (prompts, skills, tool
  descriptions, tool results, how history is sent), run the live prompt suite
  (`tests/project_prompt/README.md`, and `tests/printer_prompt` when printer
  chats changed). Its `claude-cli` backend costs no API money. Any run that
  spends API money needs Kenneth's yes first.

Report each failure with its output. A failure in the range is a bug to fix
on `jusprin-dev` before the release, not a reason to skip the step.

## 7. Guide check

Follow "Before a release" in `docs/guide/README.md`, on the build from step 6
with the new version already in `Version.hpp`.

1. Tell Kenneth first: the command drives the app on this computer's screen
   for about a minute a page, so nobody should use the computer meanwhile.
2. Run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` and fix what it reports until it
   passes. It then writes the version to `docs/guide/checked-version.txt`.
3. Look through `git log <range> -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin` for new screens or
   menu items no page mentions, and add them to the guide.

## 8. Commit and land

1. Commit the version, the notes, the catalogs and the guide files on your
   branch. Make sure no temporary working docs or screenshots are in it.
2. With Kenneth's yes, land it on `jusprin-dev` without a merge commit: rebase
   onto `origin/jusprin-dev`, then `git push origin HEAD:jusprin-dev`. Then
   bring the main checkout along: `git -C <main checkout> pull --ff-only`.
3. With Kenneth's yes, move `main` to the same commit:
   `git push origin origin/jusprin-dev:main`. This only succeeds as a fast
   forward. If it is refused, stop and tell Kenneth. Never force it.

## 9. Start the release workflow

Only Kenneth's GitHub account may run it; check with `gh api user -q .login`.
With his yes:

```bash
gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true
```

Keep Mac signing on: Homebrew refuses a Mac app that is not signed and
notarised. Wait for the run in the background (`gh run watch <id>`). A failed
run is a failure to report with its log, not a reason to tick a skip box.

## 10. Test the draft

The draft holds the Windows installer and portable zip, the Mac disk image,
the Linux AppImage and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. These files are what people will get,
so test them, not a local build. Ask Kenneth before downloading them.

On each platform: install over the previous release and start the app. Check
that Preferences shows the new version, sign in, have one chat, slice, and
check each fix in the notes on the platform where it mattered (for example a
locale bug on Windows, where it always shows). Send one error report if the
release changed reporting.

Tell Kenneth what was tested on which platform and what was not. He publishes.

## 11. After publishing

- Reply to and close the GitHub issues the release fixes, with Kenneth's yes.
- Update JusPrin's Homebrew cask to the new version, if the cask is in
  Homebrew.
- The next day, run the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise
  repository for new failures from the new version.
- Remove your worktree and branch.

30	**Never publish the draft.** Kenneth publishes it by hand on the Releases page.
31	Never force-push `main`.
32	
33	## 1. Set up
34	
35	1. Check that the main checkout (the folder that holds `jusprin-dev`, not a
36	   worktree) has nothing that would be left out of the release:
37	
38	   ```bash
39	   git -C <main checkout> fetch origin
40	   git -C <main checkout> status --porcelain -uno
41	   git -C <main checkout> log --oneline origin/jusprin-dev..jusprin-dev
42	   ```
43	
44	   Both must print nothing. A changed file or a commit that is not on GitHub
45	   is work someone may expect in the release. Stop, list each one for
46	   Kenneth, and wait until he has pushed it or said to leave it out. Do not
47	   push, commit or discard it yourself. Untracked files do not block: they
48	   are working docs Kenneth keeps there on purpose.
49	2. Find the last release: `git tag --list 'jusprin/v*' --sort=-v:refname | head -1`.
50	   The range is that tag to `origin/jusprin-dev` (after `git fetch origin`).
51	3. Make your own worktree from `origin/jusprin-dev`, under
52	   `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`, on a branch named `claude/release-<version>`.
53	   Never name it `jusprin-release/...`: pushing a branch with that name starts
54	   an unsigned release build.
55	4. Read every commit in the range: `git log --format='%h %s%n%b' <range>`.
56	   Note what a person would notice, and the GitHub issues each change fixes.
57	
58	## 2. Version and release notes
59	
60	1. Set `kVersion` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`. It must be
61	   above every released JusPrin version.
62	2. Write `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`. The app
63	   shows this file under "What's new", and the draft starts with it. Follow the
64	   shape of the previous release's file. Write for a person who prints, not for
65	   a developer. Check every on-screen label you quote against the source
66	   (`git grep`), and leave out anything you have not checked.
67	3. A change that sends anything new from the person's computer, such as a new
68	   message to our server, goes in the notes and says what it holds.
69	
70	## 3. Server readiness
71	
72	The app calls JusPrin's server at `https://jusprinv2.obico.io`. Every address
73	the release calls must already be deployed there.
74	
75	```bash
76	git grep -h -o '"/ent/jusprin/v2/[a-z_/]*' -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin ':!*test*' | tr -d '"' | sort -u
77	```
78	
79	GET each one: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://jusprinv2.obico.io<path>`.
80	Any answer but 404 (200, 401, 403, 405) means the address is there. A 404
81	means it is not deployed. Find the server change in the tsd-enterprise
82	repository (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py` on `master`), tell Kenneth what is
83	missing, and wait until it is deployed. Also tell him about any other server
84	behavior a change in the range relies on, such as a new error code.
85	
86	## 4. Translations
87	
88	1. Run `python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py`. It
89	   needs GNU gettext and `npm ci` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`. If it
90	   changes any catalog, those changes go into the release commit.
91	2. Translate every new entry in every language, following "Localization &
92	   translations" in `AGENTS.md` and the `orca-translations` skill.
93	3. `npx vitest run src/catalogs.test.ts` in `AgentUI` must pass: it fails
94	   while an entry is untranslated or a translation lost a placeholder.
95	4. Count the entries marked `# Needs human review` in
96	   `Localization/native/*.po` and `Localization/pages/*.po`. Tell Kenneth the
97	   count, so he can decide whether someone should read a language.
98	
99	These steps cannot find a sentence nobody marked for translation. While
100	reading the range, look for text a person reads that is not marked.
101	
102	## 5. Error-handling audit
103	
104	Run the `error-handling` skill on the range. When the release relies on
105	server changes, audit the tsd-enterprise range too. Report the findings to
106	Kenneth. A fix lands on `jusprin-dev` as its own commit, and the steps above
107	are then repeated for the new range.
108	
109	## 6. Tests
110	
111	Build in your worktree, in Release, following "Building on a shared machine"
112	in `AGENTS.md`: check the load first, use `-j4`, choose every target before
113	you start. Configure with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON`.
114	
115	- macOS: build `agent_bridge_tests`, `jusprin_tests`, `shell_integration_harness`,
116	  `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs`, then run both test programs and
117	  `npm test` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI`.
118	- Windows and Linux: the release workflow compiles them but runs no tests.
119	  Run `agent_bridge_tests` and `jusprin_tests` on each. Kenneth keeps test
120	  machines for both; ask him for access if you do not have it, and say in
121	  your report if they were not run.
122	- When the range changes text the model reads (prompts, skills, tool
123	  descriptions, tool results, how history is sent), run the live prompt suite
124	  (`tests/project_prompt/README.md`, and `tests/printer_prompt` when printer
125	  chats changed). Its `claude-cli` backend costs no API money. Any run that
126	  spends API money needs Kenneth's yes first.
127	
128	Report each failure with its output. A failure in the range is a bug to fix
129	on `jusprin-dev` before the release, not a reason to skip the step.
130	
131	## 7. Guide check
132	
133	Follow "Before a release" in `docs/guide/README.md`, on the build from step 6
134	with the new version already in `Version.hpp`.
135	
136	1. Tell Kenneth first: the command drives the app on this computer's screen
137	   for about a minute a page, so nobody should use the computer meanwhile.
138	2. Run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` and fix what it reports until it
139	   passes. It then writes the version to `docs/guide/checked-version.txt`.
140	3. Look through `git log <range> -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin` for new screens or
141	   menu items no page mentions, and add them to the guide.
142	
143	## 8. Commit and land
144	
145	1. Commit the version, the notes, the catalogs and the guide files on your
146	   branch. Make sure no temporary working docs or screenshots are in it.
147	2. With Kenneth's yes, land it on `jusprin-dev` without a merge commit: rebase
148	   onto `origin/jusprin-dev`, then `git push origin HEAD:jusprin-dev`. Then
149	   bring the main checkout along: `git -C <main checkout> pull --ff-only`.
150	3. With Kenneth's yes, move `main` to the same commit:
151	   `git push origin origin/jusprin-dev:main`. This only succeeds as a fast
152	   forward. If it is refused, stop and tell Kenneth. Never force it.
153	
154	## 9. Start the release workflow
155	
156	Only Kenneth's GitHub account may run it; check with `gh api user -q .login`.
157	
158	First check that the repository has the five Sentry secrets:
159	`gh secret list` must list `JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN` (the project the app sends
160	reports to), `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG` and
161	`SENTRY_PROJECT` (which upload the debug files and page source maps that
162	let Sentry name the functions in a stack, with file and line). The workflow refuses to start without them. Only
163	Kenneth can add one; tell him which is missing.
164	
165	With his yes:
166	
167	```bash
168	gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true
169	```
170	
171	Keep Mac signing on: Homebrew refuses a Mac app that is not signed and
172	notarised. Wait for the run in the background (`gh run watch <id>`). A failed
173	run is a failure to report with its log, not a reason to tick a skip box.
174	
175	## 10. Test the draft
176	
177	The draft holds the Windows installer and portable zip, the Mac disk image,
178	the Linux AppImage and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. These files are what people will get,
179	so test them, not a local build. Ask Kenneth before downloading them.
180	
181	On each platform: install over the previous release and start the app. Check
182	that Preferences shows the new version, sign in, have one chat, slice, and
183	check each fix in the notes on the platform where it mattered (for example a
184	locale bug on Windows, where it always shows).
185	
186	Check that Sentry can read this release's stacks, on the draft's own files.
187	Both scripts need `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT` and a Sentry
188	token that can read the project in `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, and only read.
189	
190	- Run `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh verify <file>`
191	  on the Mac app's `Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer` (it checks both
192	  architectures), Windows' `OrcaSlicer.dll` and the AppImage's
193	  `bin/orca-slicer` (`--appimage-extract` puts it under `squashfs-root`).
194	  Each must print "Sentry holds debug information".
195	- Run `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh verify <folder>`
196	  from the release commit, with the folder that holds `jusprin/agent` and
197	  `jusprin/home` in each platform's app: the Mac app's `Contents/Resources`,
198	  the Windows install's `resources`, the AppImage's `squashfs-root/resources`.
199	  Each must print "Sentry holds the agent page's source map" and the same
200	  for home.
201	- Send one error report from the installed app and open it in Sentry
202	  (the project `SENTRY_PROJECT` names, filter
203	  `release:"<the app line it shows>"`): the
204	  frames of the app's own code must show function names with file and line,
205	  not only addresses.
206	
207	Tell Kenneth what was tested on which platform and what was not. He publishes.
208	
209	## 11. After publishing
210	
211	- Start the previous release on one computer and check that Preferences ›
212	  Updates offers the new version. The update check reads only published
213	  releases, so this is the first moment it can be checked.
214	- Reply to and close the GitHub issues the release fixes, with Kenneth's yes.
215	- Update JusPrin's Homebrew cask to the new version, if the cask is in
216	  Homebrew.
217	- Open the newest events in Sentry for the new release and check that a
218	  report's or crash's stack names the app's functions with file and line,
219	  and that a page error's frames name the page's source files
220	  (`HomeUI/src/...`, `AgentUI/src/...`). A stack of bare addresses or of
221	  `app:///home/index.html` positions means a platform's debug files or a
222	  page's map are missing: run `sentry_debug_files.sh verify` or
223	  `sentry_page_maps.sh verify` on that platform's released files.
224	- The next day, run the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise
225	  repository for new failures from the new version.
226	- Remove your worktree and branch.

commit c27fdcbfebe5cdd493a01ede9a6299e10b9957d1
Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Nov 17 15:59:08 2026 -0800

    Send error reports and crashes straight to Sentry, with readable stacks
    
    The app's error reports used to go to JusPrin's server as five short text
    fields, which passed them on to Sentry. They now go straight from the app
    to Sentry through Sentry's own SDKs, and crashes are caught too. Kenneth:
    "We want the Sentry server to capture as much info as possible so that we
    can do production troubleshooting."
    
    What a report carries now
    - The app uses sentry-native 0.17.5 (deps/Sentry) with the crashpad
      backend. Crashpad writes a crash's minidump from its own process,
      crashpad_handler, which ships beside the app on every platform. The SDK
      hands each envelope to OrcaSlicer's own HTTP client, which already knows
      the system's certificates and proxy.
    - Nothing leaves without consent (the SDK's require_user_consent). With
      automatic reports on, reports and crashes go as they happen. With them
      off, only the one report the person chose to send goes; a crash stays on
      disk.
    - Each event has what the SDK collects: the stack, the loaded modules, the
      machine, the recent steps (each page message's type and each tool call's
      outcome, never a payload), and this run's log file. It is filed by
      release, by what the app was doing and by the system, and grouped
      without the request ids that differ every time one failure happens.
    - The stack is where the exception was thrown, not where the top handler
      reported it (Support/ThrowStack): the app's own __cxa_throw records
      each throw on macOS and Linux, and a vectored exception handler does it
      on Windows.
    - The report's two older trims are deleted: the home folder is no longer
      replaced by "~", and fields are no longer cut to the old server's
      limits. Kenneth: "delete both older trims. no need to have these
      sentences be rewritten. they were close enough that we can tweak sentry
      server settings to meet them. No need to test the rules now."
    
    The Agent and Home pages
    - Each page builds its event with @sentry/browser 11.10.0 and hands it to
      the app in its report_error message; the page itself never reaches the
      network for this. The app sends it like its own reports.
    - On macOS and Linux the pages now load from jusprin:///<page>/index.html,
      served from resources/jusprin by a scheme handler each web view
      registers (Support/PageScheme). WKWebView and WebKitGTK tell a file://
      page only "Script error." about an uncaught error, with no file, line or
      stack, and Sentry's SDK drops that, so these errors never reached
      Sentry. The handler names each file's content type itself: on Linux,
      wxWidgets labels .html as application/xhtml+xml, and WebKitGTK would
      parse the page as XML. Windows keeps file://, where WebView2 reports the
      whole error.
    - All web views share one handler, which lives as long as the app. On
      macOS wxWidgets gives WKWebView only a plain pointer to the handler, and
      WebKit can still ask it for a file after the view that registered it is
      gone; with a handler per view, the shell harness crashed there.
    - Visible effect: on macOS and Linux, an uncaught page error that used to
      vanish now opens the "Something went wrong on our side" dialog, or is
      sent at once when automatic reports are on.
    - Frames name the page the same way everywhere, app:///<page>/index.html,
      so one source map per page serves every platform. A Vite plugin writes
      that map for the script vite-plugin-singlefile inlines into index.html.
      New .gitattributes files keep the pages' sources in LF on every
      checkout, so every platform builds the same page.
    
    Release and nightly builds
    - The build's DSN comes from the JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN repository secret, so
      this public repository names no production host. A build without it
      sends nothing.
    - macOS and Linux builds add line tables (-gline-tables-only) and split
      them off: a dSYM on macOS, a .debug file matched by GNU build id on
      Linux. Each platform uploads its debug files (PDBs on Windows) and the
      pages' source maps, and fails unless Sentry then holds debug information
      with file and line for the app's own code
      (Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh) and a map for each page
      (Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh). The release workflow refuses to start
      without the five Sentry secrets. The release skill and AGENTS.md
      "Releasing" say how to check a draft's files.
    
    OrcaSlicer-owned files
    - deps/CMakeLists.txt: two added lines that include and list the Sentry
      dependency.

#

#       functions only, so it does not count. The release skill runs it on a
#       released copy of the app.

It doesn't.** The release build commands (`build_win.bat -s -i`, `build_linux.sh -srlL`) pass no test flag, so nothing shows the tests even compile there. The skill now gives the test commands for each platform: `build_win.bat -s --tests` and `./build_linux.sh -st`.

**The smaller fixes:**
- **Server addresses:** the address search missed every address the app joins from pieces, such as `/o/token/`, `/accounts/...`, `/models` and each sign-in step. The new search finds them, plus one the reviewer also missed (`/o/revoke_token/`).

content.text:
The second review ([Second cold read of the jusprin-release skill](#local_2a1fa767-23d6-41a2-92fd-1e91eb21e28c)) found nothing that would ship a release without your yes. It confirmed that every target, path and flag the skill names exists. Its most serious finding was that the skill ran only 2 of JusPrin's 9 test programs. I checked each finding against the files and fixed them all, plus one the reviewer misread.

**Main fixes**
- **Every test program now runs.** The skill builds all the test programs and runs every suite registered with the test runner, OrcaSlicer's included. The skipped ones included the update-check tests, which cover the very code that offers a new release to people. The live AI tests are built but never run automatically, since each run costs API money.
- **When a test fails,** the agent first runs that test on a build of the last release. If it fails there too, the agent reports it as an older problem and you decide.
- **New section on what to do after a fix.** The fix is its own commit on `jusprin-dev`, and pushing it needs your yes. Then the agent rebases and redoes the server check, the audit, the tests, the translations and the guide check. The audit and the tests now run before the translations, because a fix from either can add a sentence that needs translating.
- **Commits that land mid-release now wait for your answer.** If you say no, the release stops. Before, the agent rebased onto them without waiting.

**The one the reviewer misread**
- It said maintenance mode makes the server answer 5xx. It doesn't: in tsd-enterprise, `web_ent/urls_ent.py` answers 200 with the same page for every path, so every address check would pass. The skill now first requests a made-up address, which must answer 404, and stops on any 5xx.

**Smaller fixes**
- The version is settled before the worktree branch named after it is made.
- The release notes text was wrong: the app has no "What's new". An older app shows the release text under "Release notes" in Preferences › Updates.
- The run id is now taken from the run created after starting the workflow, not simply the newest.
- The publisher variable can't be read from this computer, and the skill now says what to do if the run's first job refuses the account.
- The Sentry checks now say which machine runs which part, and give the exact release name to search for.

**One thing you should know:** the Homebrew pull request for JusPrin (Homebrew/homebrew-cask#303257) was closed on 2026-11-17 without being merged. So there's no JusPrin cask in Homebrew right now. The skill's Homebrew step now applies only once a cask exists, and opening a pull request there needs your yes.

Both rounds of skill fixes are committed on local `jusprin-dev` as 7dee738e40 and 455db3d9de, not pushed.

input.prompt:
Review the `jusprin-release` skill (`.claude/skills/jusprin-release/SKILL.md`) as a cold reader. Judge whether an agent that has only this skill and the repository could make a new JusPrin release without missing a step or getting confused.

This is a read-only review. Do not run any step of the skill. That means no builds, no version bumps, no commits, no pushes, no workflow runs, no catalog updates, and no requests to servers. Read-only `git` and `gh` queries are fine, and so is reading the tsd-enterprise repository at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`. Edit no files in either checkout. Other sessions use them.

Check every command, path, target, flag, label and claim in the skill against the files it relies on. Verify each by reading the file or with `git grep`, not from memory. Those files include:
- `AGENTS.md` and `tests/AGENTS.md`
- `.github/workflows/jusprin_*.yml` and `winget_updater.yml`
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/`
- `docs/guide/README.md` and `scripts/check_guide.py`
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/README.md`
- the `error-handling` skill
- `tests/project_prompt/README.md`
- `tests/CMakeLists.txt` and the test folders
- `build_win.bat` and `build_linux.sh`
- the code that builds server addresses (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/`)

Look for these kinds of problems:
- Steps that are missing, or steps in the wrong order.
- Wrong or nonexistent commands, targets or flags. That includes commands an agent's shell would refuse.
- Places where an agent would have to guess, including what to do when a step fails.
- Claims about what a workflow or script does that are false.
- Anything that would make the agent act without Kenneth's yes where he must approve.
- Text that is unclear or contradicts itself.

Done looks like a report in your final message, under about 600 words. List each finding most serious first. For each one, give the skill's line, what goes wrong for the agent following it, and a suggested rewording. Mark each finding as verified or inferred. If nothing serious is left, say so plainly and first. End with what you could not check without running something.
input.background: JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer: a C++ desktop slicer with wxWidgets, plus two web pages built with Vite and React. `jusprin-dev` is the development branch. `main` is the stable and release branch, and is never force-pushed. The last published release is 2.0.0, tagged `jusprin/v2.0.0`. Kenneth owns the project. He alone may start the release workflow, deploy the server, approve pushes and publish. The `jusprin-release` skill lists every step of a release, including steps the release workflow does not enforce. Two earlier cold reads found gaps, which were fixed in commits `7dee738e40` and `455db3d9de` on local `jusprin-dev`. Neither commit is pushed. This third reader has never seen the skill. The aim is to confirm the skill is now complete and unambiguous, or to find what is still wrong, before anyone uses it for a real release.

---
name: windows-gui-test-vm-gcp
description: Working recipe for testing the OrcaSlicer/JusPrin GUI headlessly on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP, and the four traps that make it fail silently.
metadata:
  type: project
---

A Windows GUI test VM for this app works in GCP with no GPU. Instance
`jusprin-win-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-central1-a`,
n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB, Cascade Lake), 500 GB pd-balanced,
Windows Server 2022. Harness + full README live outside the repo
at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/vm-harness/windows/`. Verified 2026-09-07 end to end:
launch, screenshot, scripted click, verify the UI advanced.

**Why:** four failure modes here are silent — they look like "the app has no
window" or "the app hung" rather than reporting an error, so they cost hours if
rediscovered from scratch.

**How to apply:**
- OpenGL: the app hard-requires 3.2 and Windows software rendering is 1.1. Drop
  Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` beside the .exe. Then force
  `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` — otherwise Mesa picks
  its d3d12 backend (the GCE virtual display exposes a D3D12 device) and crashes
  on the first frame.
- Never copy the whole Mesa .7z to the VM: Defender deletes it as
  Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere, copy only those, and
  no AV exclusion is needed.
- Session isolation is the big one: display APIs, EnumWindows and
  MainWindowTitle only see the calling session's window station, so over SSH they
  report nothing and it reads as "no window exists". Run anything UI-touching as a
  scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive`.
- Auto-logon must be re-applied on every boot; the GCE image clears the Winlogon
  values after the boot that sets them.
- Resolution needs `gcloud compute instances update --enable-display-device`
  (instance must be stopped) or you get 640x480, smaller than the app's own window.
- WebView2 runtime is absent on a clean Windows Server image; without it the app
  blocks on a modal prompt at startup. Matters especially for JusPrin's
  WebView-based UI. See [[jusprin-rebrand-seams]].

Claude Code and the Claude desktop app are both installed for `guitest`
(2026-09-08). CLI: the native Windows installer `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1`
puts `claude.exe` in `C:\Users\guitest\.local\bin` - no Node needed, the box has
none. Desktop app: install with Anthropic's own Intune script,
`https://downloads.claude.ai/releases/enterprise/intune/Install-Claude.ps1 -Scope User`,
which resolves the official MSIX and verifies its signature and publisher identity.
MSIX deployment works on this Windows Server 2022 image. Launch the packaged app in
session 1 through explorer.exe, so it lands at normal integrity even though the
scheduled task is elevated:
`Invoke-InSession -Exe C:\Windows\explorer.exe -ArgLine "shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude"`.
Electron renders fine on this GPU-less VM with no flags.

RDP: port 3389 is open project-wide via `default-allow-rdp` (to 0.0.0.0/0 - not
narrowed yet), and RDP as `guitest` reconnects to the existing console session
rather than starting a second one. Run `./get-rdp-password.sh` in the harness to
print the current credentials; it resolves the ephemeral IP itself and verifies
the password actually authenticates before handing it to you. Do NOT use
`gcloud compute reset-windows-password` - autologon.ps1 re-syncs the account to
Winlogon\DefaultPassword at the next boot and would undo it.

autologon.ps1 used to mint a NEW random password on every boot, so any reboot
silently invalidated the RDP credentials. Fixed 2026-09-09: it now reuses the
stored DefaultPassword and only generates one when that value is absent (delete
the value and reboot to rotate deliberately). This matters because Windows
Update on this VM is set to install and restart on its own, daily at 3 AM, and
the box has also rebooted unexpectedly several times - Kernel-Power event 41,
cause not established.

Two mechanical traps: nested quoting through `winssh.sh` into `powershell -Command`
mangles almost anything non-trivial - write a .ps1, scp it, run it with `-File`.
And a PATH change made over SSH does not reach session 1's already-running Explorer;
re-set the variable from inside the session and restart Explorer, or a new terminal
there still will not find the command.

Tuned 2026-09-08, both changes measured. Windows Defender had real-time scanning
on with zero exclusions, so it scanned every object file the compiler wrote.
Excluding C:\src, C:\tools, C:\guitest plus the compiler binaries took a
small-file write benchmark from 545 to 983 files/s and reads from 979 to 2257 -
roughly 1.8x and 2.3x, for free. Re-add these if the VM is ever rebuilt.

The boot disk was grown 100 -> 500 GB. On GCE a balanced persistent disk's speed
scales with its provisioned size (140 MB/s + 0.28 per GB), so the old 100 GB disk
was capped at 168 MB/s - it was slow *because* it was small. Aggregate write went
from that 168 ceiling to a measured 262 MB/s. Resize is online: `gcloud compute
disks resize`, then `Resize-Partition` on disk 0 partition 3; C: is the last
partition so nothing blocks the extend, and no reboot is needed.

**Do not benchmark GCE persistent disk with one synchronous writer.** A single
WriteThrough stream is latency-bound and reported only 185 MB/s on the 500 GB
disk, which reads as 'the resize did nothing'. Eight concurrent writers showed the
real 262 MB/s. Use concurrent writers - that is also what a parallel build does.

RDP now prefers the H.264 codec: AVC444ModePreferred=1 (DWORD) under
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services, effective on the
next connection. That does not touch the real interactivity limit, which is the
~57 ms round-trip from California to us-central1; only moving the VM to a west
coast region fixes that.

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on every stop/start.

**Why:** the traps below each cost a retry.

**How to apply:**
- `ai-agent` cannot attach the default compute service account; create VMs with
  `--no-service-account --no-scopes`.
- xrdp is bound to 127.0.0.1 and reached through an SSH tunnel (connect-rdp.sh,

- The repo is private: send code as a git bundle. A bundle of `origin/jusprin-dev`
  stores `refs/remotes/origin/jusprin-dev`, so `git clone -b jusprin-dev` fails;
  fetch that ref explicitly.
- Set `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` or the app blocks at
  startup on a certificate-store dialog.
- After a start, xrdp can fail at boot (2026-11-11): systemd times out waiting
  for /run/xrdp/xrdp.pid, the folder is gone, and the tunnel prints "channel 2:
  open failed: connect failed: Connection refused". Fix:
  `sudo systemctl restart xrdp-sesman xrdp`, then `ss -ltn | grep 3389`.
- `pkill -f orca-slicer` over ssh kills the ssh session itself; use `pkill -x`.
- Homebrew moved openssl@3 to @4 on 2026-11-09 and broke gcloud's Python;
  env.sh sets CLOUDSDK_PYTHON to uv's standalone CPython 3.12.
- Landed 2026-11-09 as fdb873ad65 on jusprin-dev: the Linux test-configure fix
  (name the target in six `orcaslicer_copy_test_dlls()` calls), the CLI crash on a
  filament without filament_diameter, and the Orca account file-time fix. Full
  Linux ctest then passes. VM checkout is on jusprin-dev at that commit.
- Linking tests/jusprin can race: shell_theme_tests and jusprin_fake_bambu_tests
  both copy the Python runtime into Release/python ("Error removing directory").

2.0.1

JusPrin 2.0.1 speaks your language, connects more printers from the printer chat, and fixes printers that could not be added in languages that write decimals with a comma.

## New

- **JusPrin in your language.** JusPrin's own screens, the AI chat and Home are translated into the 22 languages OrcaSlicer ships. Choose the language in Preferences › Appearance › Language. Numbers follow it too, for example "0,4 mm" in German. The translations are made by machine, so some wording may read oddly.
- **More printers connect from the printer chat.** The printer chat can now connect every connection type OrcaSlicer's printer settings offer, not only Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint. This includes Elegoo Centauri Carbon and Centauri Carbon 2 printers (Elegoo Link). The chat cannot finish Repetier, UltiMaker, or PrusaLink with a user name and password, and tells you where to set those up instead. Obico, SimplyPrint and 3DPrinterOS still need their own sign-in.
- **Reporting errors.** When something goes wrong that you can't fix yourself, JusPrin shows one message, "Something went wrong on our side". You can see the whole report, then press Report to JusPrin team, or tick "From now on, report errors like this automatically". You can also turn this on or off in Preferences › Updates › Error reports. It is off until you turn it on.

## Fixed

- In languages that write decimals with a comma, such as German, French, Spanish, Portuguese and Russian, the add-printer form showed no nozzle sizes for most printers, so the printer could not be added. Bed sizes such as 233.5 mm were also read as 233 mm, and a 0.4 mm nozzle in an opened 3MF file was read as 0. This always happened on Windows.
- A calibration test started from one of your projects lost that project and its chat.
- A project could save itself again after sitting idle, with nothing changed.
- A file the AI chat refused to attach (too large, or a kind it can't read) stopped the project from saving until you removed it.
- If JusPrin couldn't write its settings file, signing in or saving an API key looked like it worked, and was lost when you quit. JusPrin now shows an error instead.
- Deleting your account now waits until AI has finished replying in any chat.
- A chat whose account or API key was removed showed the wrong model in its greyed-out model picker. It now shows the model the chat ran on.
- When AI prepared a print, it could keep checking the slice it had just started, again and again, while the slice ran.

## What JusPrin now sends

- **When the app starts**, it tells JusPrin's server once that it started: a random number made on the first start, the app's version and the name of your operating system. Nothing in it names you, and no sign-in goes with it. It is not sent in stealth mode.
- **Error reports and crashes** go to JusPrin's error tracker (Sentry) only when you press Report to JusPrin team, or when you have turned on automatic reports. A report holds where in the app the error happened, the steps just before it (never what you typed or what AI said), your operating system and the app's log for that run. A crash report also holds the app's state at the moment it crashed. With automatic reports off, a crash report stays on your computer.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.

# Handoff: seven error-handling bugs to fix for the release after 2.0.1

Kenneth, 2026-11-17, during the 2.0.1 release: "create a handoff doc for the 7
bugs for the next release". 2.0.1 ships without these fixes.

The error-handling audit of the 2.0.1 range (tag `jusprin/v2.0.0` to
`262fe08e91`) found them. Each was found **by reading the code only**. None
has been reproduced yet. AGENTS.md's bug-fix rule applies: reproduce each one
in the local dev environment first, show it failing, then fix it and show it
passing. If one cannot be reproduced, stop and tell Kenneth instead of fixing
it. Each fix is its own commit on a branch from `origin/jusprin-dev`, and the
error-handling rules in AGENTS.md ("Error handling") decide what the fixed code
may do.

The line numbers are from `262fe08e91`. They may have moved since.

The audit also found about 20 smaller rule findings, in the app and in the
server: sentences or codes for failures nobody decided. They are listed in
`/Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_55a7089d-34d6-4d0c-bc2e-c3745b488d0d/release-2.0.1-audit-findings.md`
