## 1. The error report promises less than it sends

**What the person sees.** The "Something went wrong on our side" dialog says
the report is only the lines shown: "That is the whole report. It has no chat
messages, no files, no project names and no account or email address."
Preferences › Updates › Error reports says the same and adds "JusPrin's server
sees your IP address, as with any web page."

**What is actually sent.** Since a14e9d762f (reports go straight to Sentry)
every report also carries this run's log file
(`Support/SentryClient.cpp:159-166`), the native stack, the loaded modules
and the machine. The home folder is no longer replaced by "~", and the report
goes to Sentry, not JusPrin's server. For the app's own reports the dialog's
"Where" row is empty, so it says "That is the whole report" while a stack and
the log go with it. The log can name project files and folders.

**Where.** `Shell/ErrorReportDialog.cpp:116-117, 141-143, 225-234`,
`AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:657`.

**Needs Kenneth.** This is a wording decision or a decision about what to
send, not a code fix alone. His earlier "Keep the promise and accept the
risk" (b3eed3bf4b) was about error text, before the log was attached. Bring
him the choice: make the sentences say what is sent (new wording, translated
into the 22 languages), or send less (no log file, home folder trimmed again,
which he had removed: "delete both older trims"). Do not pick for him.
Before writing any sentence that says what a report never holds, check what
the log file can contain.

## 2. An AI reply can spin forever

**What the person sees.** The reply spinner never stops, and the chat stays
busy until they press Stop. With automatic reports on, no dialog opens, so
nothing tells them anything.

**Cause found by reading.** Only `pump_stream`'s handler
(`Agent/AgentHost.cpp:3442`) ends a reply as failed. Two other paths can
throw without ending it:
- starting the request: `begin_stream` calls `m_agent->start` at
  `AgentHost.cpp:3034`, which can throw from `post()`
  (`ProviderAgent.cpp:462`) or from `keep_blob`'s write;
- continuing after a tool result: `continue_after_tool`
  (`AgentHost.cpp:3410`) can throw from `next_call` (`ProviderAgent.cpp:585`)
  or its `post()`.

The throw reaches the page-message handler or the shell timer's
`reported(...)`, is reported under the wrong "was doing", and `fail_stream`
never runs, so `m_stream` stays set.

## 3. A printer card on Home can freeze for the rest of the run

**What the person sees.** One printer's card on Home stops updating and shows
its last reading until the app restarts. Quitting waits 3 seconds.

**Cause found by reading.** `Printers/HostLaneReader.cpp:213-216` wraps the
read thread in `reported()`. If `read()` throws, `shared->finish(...)` and
`--running` are skipped. The printer stays marked in flight, so `begin()`
never reads it again this run. The failure is reported once.

255	   check changed in `docs/guide/` (pages, `pictures/`, `checked-version.txt`)
256	   and the guide skills it rebuilt in `AgentUI/src/skills/guide-*/`. Make

264	   your branch cannot reach `jusprin-dev` without those commits.

266	   `git push origin HEAD:jusprin-dev`. Then bring the main checkout along:
267	   `git -C <main checkout> pull --ff-only`. If that pull is refused, someone
268	   committed in the main checkout meanwhile: stop and tell Kenneth, and do not
269	   change the main checkout. Write down your commit
270	   (`git rev-parse HEAD`). This is the release commit.
271	4. With Kenneth's yes, move `main` to that exact commit:
272	   `git push origin <release commit>:main`. This only succeeds as a fast
273	   forward. If it is refused, stop and tell Kenneth. Never force it.
274	
275	## 9. Start the release workflow
276	
277	Only the release publisher may run it: the repository variable
278	`JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER`, or `kennethjiang` when that is unset. The `gh`
279	token on this computer may not be allowed to read the variable (`gh variable
280	list` can answer 403). Check that `gh api user -q .login` prints
281	`kennethjiang`. If the run's first job fails with "Only @<name> may make a

283	
284	The workflow refuses to start without five Sentry secrets:
285	`JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN` (the project the app sends reports to), and
286	`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT` (which

288	functions in a stack, with file and line). The `gh` token on this computer

291	can add it.
292	
293	With his yes:
294	
295	```bash
296	gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true
297	gh run list --workflow jusprin_release.yml --limit 3 --json databaseId,headSha,createdAt,event
298	```
299	
300	Run the second command about 15 seconds after the first: a new run takes a
301	few seconds to appear. Take the `workflow_dispatch` run
302	created after you started it, and check that its `headSha` is the release
303	commit. Keep Mac signing on:

305	in the background (`gh run watch <databaseId>`). If its "Upload to the draft
306	release" job waits for an approval (the `release` environment can require
307	one), tell Kenneth. A failed run is a failure to report with its log, not a
308	reason to tick a skip box.
309	
310	## 10. Test the draft
311	
312	The draft holds the Windows installer and portable zip, the Mac disk image,
313	the Linux AppImage and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. These files are what people will get,
314	so test them, not a local build. Ask Kenneth before downloading them.
315	
316	On each platform: the Mac disk image on this computer, and the Windows
317	installer and the AppImage on their VMs. Install over the previous release
318	and start the app. Check
319	that Preferences shows the new version. Kenneth signs in, or you use a test
320	account he names: never type a password yourself. Have one chat (it spends
321	that account's credits), slice, and
322	check each fix in the notes on the platform where it mattered (for example a
323	locale bug on Windows, where it always shows).
324	
325	Check that Sentry can read this release's stacks, on the draft's own files.
326	Run both scripts from your release worktree on the Mac, for the Mac disk
327	image and for the Windows portable zip unpacked there (its `JusPrin/` folder
328	holds `OrcaSlicer.dll` and `resources`). Run the AppImage's part on the Linux
329	VM, in a checkout of the release commit with node and npx:
330	`--appimage-extract` only works on Linux.
331	Both scripts read `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT` and
332	`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` from the environment. GitHub secrets cannot be read back,
333	so ask Kenneth for the values and for a token that can only read the
334	project. Set them in the shell for these commands only, and never write
335	them into a file.
336	
337	- Run `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh verify <file>`
338	  on the Mac app's `Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer` (it checks both
339	  architectures), Windows' `OrcaSlicer.dll` and the AppImage's
340	  `bin/orca-slicer` (`--appimage-extract` puts it under `squashfs-root`).
341	  Each must print "Sentry holds debug information".
342	- Run `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh verify <folder>`
343	  from the release commit, with the folder that holds `jusprin/agent` and
344	  `jusprin/home` in each platform's app: the Mac app's `Contents/Resources`,
345	  the unpacked Windows zip's `JusPrin/resources`, the AppImage's `squashfs-root/resources`.
346	  Each must print "Sentry holds the agent page's source map" and the same
347	  for home.
348	- If an unexpected error happens while you test, send its report and open
349	  it in Sentry (the project `SENTRY_PROJECT` names, filtered by
350	  `release:"JusPrin <version> (OrcaSlicer <SoftFever_VERSION>)"`, the name
351	  `Updates::version_label()` gives, with `SoftFever_VERSION` from

355	  report. If none happens, say this check was not done; the two scripts

358	Before Kenneth publishes, check `gh workflow list --all | grep -i winget`.
359	`winget_updater.yml` is inherited from OrcaSlicer. It runs when a release is

363	
364	Tell Kenneth what was tested on which platform and what was not. He publishes.
365	
366	## 11. After publishing
367	
368	- Start the previous release on one computer and check that Preferences ›
369	  Updates offers the new version. The update check reads only published
370	  releases, so this is the first moment it can be checked.

---
name: jusprin-release
description: Use when asked to make, prepare or start a new JusPrin release (a new version on GitHub), from choosing the commit range to the after-publish steps. Covers the version, release notes, server readiness, translations, the error-handling audit, tests, the guide check, moving main, the release workflow, testing the draft and what follows publishing. Not for JusPrin 1 (jusprin-v1) or OrcaSlicer's own releases.
---

# Making a JusPrin release

`.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml` builds one commit into a draft
release. It refuses the commit without a new version, release notes, a guide
check and the Sentry secrets (see "Releasing" in `AGENTS.md`). It does not
run tests, check the server, check translations or audit error handling.
This skill covers all of it, in order.

## Kenneth decides these

Ask, and wait for his yes before each one. A yes covers that action only.

- The version, when he has not named it, and the release notes' wording.
- Deploying the server.
- Which error-handling findings must be fixed before the release.
- Taking in commits that landed on `jusprin-dev` after the range was fixed.
- Spending API money (say the cost).
- Every push, and moving `main`.
- Starting the release workflow.
- Downloading the draft's files.
- The Sentry values and read-only token for checking the draft.
- Posting anything on GitHub.

Never publish the draft: Kenneth does, by hand. Never force-push `main`.

## When something has to be fixed

A fix is its own commit on `jusprin-dev`, made in a worktree of its own from
`origin/jusprin-dev`, never in the release commit. Once it is pushed:

- **Before section 8 landed the release commit:** rebase your branch onto
  `origin/jusprin-dev`, record that as the new end of the range, and redo
  step 1.4 and sections 2 to 7.
- **After it landed:** keep the version. Redo step 1.4 and sections 2 to 7
  up to the fix, land what changed (section 8), move `main` and start the
  workflow again. A new run for the same version replaces the draft.

## Where each platform is tested

Every release is tested on all three platforms, twice: the test suites
(section 5) and the draft's own files (section 10). An untested platform
blocks the release.

- **macOS:** this computer.
- **Windows and Linux:** the two Google Cloud test VMs. How to reach, start,
  build on and run the app on each is in
  `<main checkout>/.claude/vm-harness/windows/README.md` and `…/linux/README.md`.
  That folder is local to this computer, never in the repository. Start a
  stopped VM, and stop it again when done. If a VM or that folder is
  missing, stop and tell Kenneth.

## 1. Set up

1. The main checkout (the folder holding `jusprin-dev`) must have no changed
   tracked files and no commits missing from `origin/jusprin-dev`. If it has
   any, list them for Kenneth and wait; never push, commit or discard them
   yourself. Untracked files are his working docs and do not block.
2. The range is the newest `jusprin/v*` tag to the current
   `origin/jusprin-dev`. Record that commit: every later step checks this
   range, and section 8 checks whether `jusprin-dev` moved.
3. Settle the version, then make a worktree at that commit under
   `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`, on branch `claude/release-<version>` (add a
   suffix if taken). Never name a branch `jusprin-release/...`: pushing one
   starts an unsigned release build.
4. Read every commit in the range for what a person would notice and the
   GitHub issues it fixes.

## 2. Version and release notes

1. `kVersion` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`.
2. `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`, shaped like
   the previous one, for a person who prints. It becomes the draft's text on
   every workflow run, and an older app shows it under "Release notes" in
   Preferences › Updates. Check every on-screen label you quote against the
   source.
3. Anything new the app sends from the person's computer goes in the notes,
   with what it holds.

## 3. Server readiness

Every address the release calls must already answer on
`https://jusprinv2.obico.io`. Many are joined from pieces, so list them from
the code that builds them and write out each full path:

```bash
git grep -n -E '"/(ent|o|accounts|jusprin)/|"/models"|ask_server\("' -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin ':!*test*'
```

For example `ask_server("code/confirm", …)` is
`/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/code/confirm`, and the model list is the gateway's
address with its last part replaced by `/models`. A bare GET with no sign-in
or real data is enough.

First GET a made-up address such as `/ent/jusprin/v2/no-such-address`: it
must answer 404. In maintenance mode the server answers 200 for every path,
and the check cannot tell anything apart; stop and tell Kenneth.

A missing address means the server change is not deployed. Find it in
tsd-enterprise (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py` on `master`) and tell Kenneth,
along with any other server behavior the range relies on. Deploying is his
call.

## 4. Error-handling audit

Run the `error-handling` skill on the range. When the release relies on
server changes, also audit tsd-enterprise's `web_ent/jusprin/` commits on
`master` since the previous tag's date (that repository has no release tags).
Report the findings and wait for Kenneth to say which must be fixed.

## 5. Tests

Build in your worktree in Release, following "Building on a shared machine"
in `AGENTS.md`. Use CMake.app's cmake (Homebrew's fails to find Eigen3), node
on `PATH`, and absolute paths.

The main checkout's dependency build may predate a dependency the range
added. Sentry is one: if
`<main checkout>/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local/lib/cmake/sentry`
is missing, build only that dependency into a scratch folder and point the
app's build at it:

```bash
cmake -S <worktree>/deps -B <scratch>/depsbuild -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DDESTDIR=<scratch>/depsprefix
cmake --build <scratch>/depsbuild --target dep_Sentry -- -j4
```

```bash
cmake -S <worktree> -B <worktree>/build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<main checkout>/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -Dsentry_DIR=<scratch>/depsprefix/usr/local/lib/cmake/sentry \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
cmake --build <worktree>/build/arm64 --config Release --target tests/all jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs -- -j4
ctest --test-dir <worktree>/build/arm64/tests -C Release --output-on-failure -LE RequiresApp
```

Leave out `-Dsentry_DIR` when the main checkout's dependencies have Sentry.
`CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` takes one path only. `tests/all` builds every test
program, including `shell_integration_harness` for the guide check.
`agent_live_tests` is built but never registered with ctest, since each run
is billed. Also run `npm test` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI`.

- **Windows and Linux,** on the VMs, from a checkout of the end of the range:
  `build_win.bat -s --run-tests`, and `./build_linux.sh -st` then
  `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release --output-on-failure`, keeping the
  `RequiresApp` tests, which run only on Linux.
- **Prompt suites,** when the range changes text the model reads: run
  `tests/project_prompt` (and `tests/printer_prompt` when printer chats
  changed) on the free `claude-cli` backend. Its README also asks for a small
  paid run on the app's default model before a release; propose it with its
  cost.

To tell whether the range caused a failure, run the same test on a build of
the last release's tag. A failure there too is older: report it and let
Kenneth decide. One the range caused is a bug to fix before the release.

## 6. Translations

After the audit and tests, since a fix can add a sentence.

1. Run `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py` (needs GNU
   gettext and `npm ci` in `AgentUI`). Changed catalogs go in the release
   commit.
2. Translate new entries in JusPrin's own catalogs, `Localization/native/`
   and `Localization/pages/`, as `Localization/README.md` says. Never touch
   upstream's `localization/i18n/` or run `run_gettext`; from `AGENTS.md` and
   the `orca-translations` skill take only the editing rules and glossary.
3. `npx vitest run src/catalogs.test.ts` in `AgentUI` must pass.
4. Rebuild `jusprin_web` and `jusprin_catalogs` for the guide check.
5. Tell Kenneth how many entries are marked `# Needs human review`.

No tool finds a sentence nobody marked for translation; look for one while
reading the range.

## 7. Guide check

Follow "Before a release" in `docs/guide/README.md`, on the step 5 build.

1. Tell Kenneth first: it drives the app on this Mac's screen, and nobody
   should use the computer meanwhile.
2. Add new screens or menu items from the range to the guide before the
   check: it cannot find them, and a page changed after it passes is
   unchecked.
3. Run `<worktree>/scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. The script checks the
   tree it sits in, so the main checkout's copy checks the wrong code. It
   writes `docs/guide/checked-version.txt` when it passes.

## 8. Commit and land

1. The release commit holds `Version.hpp`, the notes, the catalogs, and what
   the guide check changed: `docs/guide/` (pages, `pictures/`,
   `checked-version.txt`) and `AgentUI/src/skills/guide-*/`. Nothing else.
2. If `origin/jusprin-dev` moved past the recorded end of the range, list the
   new commits for Kenneth. With his yes, rebase and redo step 1.4 and
   sections 2 to 7. If he says no, the release waits: your branch cannot
   reach `jusprin-dev` without them.
3. With his yes, push to `jusprin-dev` without a merge commit, then
   `git -C <main checkout> pull --ff-only`. If that pull is refused, stop and
   tell Kenneth without changing the main checkout.
4. With his yes, move `main` to that exact release commit, as a fast
   forward only.

## 9. Start the release workflow

The publisher is the repository variable `JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER`, or
`kennethjiang` when unset; `gh api user -q .login` must print it. This
computer's `gh` token cannot read repository variables or secrets (403), so
the workflow's first job is what reports a wrong publisher or a missing
Sentry secret (`JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`,
`SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`). Only Kenneth can add a secret.

With his yes:

```bash
gh workflow run jusprin_release.yml --ref main -f sign_macos=true
```

Keep Mac signing on: Homebrew refuses an unsigned Mac app. Check that the new
`workflow_dispatch` run is on the release commit. If its "Upload to the draft
release" job waits for an approval (the `release` environment can require
one), tell Kenneth. A failed run is reported with its log, never worked
around with a skip box.

## 10. Test the draft

Test the draft's own files: the Mac disk image on this computer, the Windows
installer and the AppImage on their VMs. Install over the previous release,
check that Preferences shows the new version, have one chat and slice, and
check each fix in the notes on the platform where it mattered. Kenneth signs
in, or you use a test account he names; never type a password. A chat spends
that account's credits.

Sentry must be able to read this release's stacks. Kenneth gives you
`SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT` and a read-only
`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`; set them in the shell only, never in a file. From the
release worktree, on the Mac for the disk image and the unpacked Windows
portable zip (its `JusPrin/` folder), and on the Linux VM for the AppImage
(`--appimage-extract` only works on Linux; that VM needs a checkout of the
release commit and node):

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh verify <file>` on
  the Mac app's `Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer`, Windows' `OrcaSlicer.dll` and
  the AppImage's `squashfs-root/bin/orca-slicer` must print "Sentry holds
  debug information".
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_page_maps.sh verify <folder>` on
  the Mac app's `Contents/Resources`, the Windows zip's `JusPrin/resources`
  and `squashfs-root/resources` must say Sentry holds both pages' source
  maps.
- The app cannot cause an error report on purpose, and Help › Report a
  problem opens a GitHub issue, not a Sentry report. If an unexpected error
  happens while testing, send it and check in Sentry, under release
  `JusPrin <version> (OrcaSlicer <SoftFever_VERSION from version.inc>)`, that
  the app's frames show function, file and line. Otherwise say it was not
  done.

`winget_updater.yml`, inherited from OrcaSlicer, would submit the installer
to winget as `SoftFever.OrcaSlicer` on publish. `gh workflow list --all` must
show it `disabled_manually`; if not, tell Kenneth before he publishes.

Tell Kenneth what was tested on which platform. He publishes.

## 11. After publishing

- Start the previous release and check that Preferences › Updates offers the
  new one. The update check reads only published releases.
- With Kenneth's yes, reply to and close the issues the release fixes, and
  open a Homebrew cask pull request if JusPrin's cask is in Homebrew
  (`brew info --cask jusprin`).
- In Sentry, a new report's or crash's stack must name the app's functions
  with file and line, and a page error's frames the pages' sources
  (`AgentUI/src/...`, `HomeUI/src/...`). Bare addresses or
  `app:///home/index.html` positions mean a platform's debug files or a map
  are missing: run the verify scripts on that platform's released files.
- The next day, run the `jusprin-production-check` skill in tsd-enterprise.
- Remove your worktree and branch.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lets a pull request's macOS deps build, or its clang-tidy job, wait for a
# build that saves the deps cache it needs, from a Linux job. `check` runs after
# a cache miss and names a queued or running push build of the base branch with
# the same deps/ and .github/ to wait for, unless the pull request changes either.
# `own` names the pull request's own build instead, for clang-tidy when the pull
# request changes deps/. `wait` waits until that build saves KEY under CACHE_REF,
# or its deps job fails. actions/cache then confirms the entry can be restored.
#
# Environment: GH_TOKEN, REPO, WORKFLOW_REF (or WORKFLOW, the build workflow's
# file name) and BASE_REF, plus HEAD_SHA for `own`, and KEY_INPUTS, WAIT_FOR,
# WAIT_SINCE, WAIT_MINUTES, KEY, CACHE_REF (default the base branch) and ARCH
# (or JOB, the matrix job's name) for `wait`.
# Writes key-inputs, wait-for and wait-since to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
set -uo pipefail

workflow=${WORKFLOW_REF:-}
workflow=${workflow%%@*}
workflow=${WORKFLOW:-${workflow##*/}}

# Must match the job names in build_all.yml, build_check_cache.yml and build_deps.yml.
job=${JOB:-build_macos_arch (${ARCH:-})}
check_job_name="$job / Check Cache"
deps_job_name="$job / Build Deps / Build Deps"

out() { echo "$1" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-/dev/stdout}"; }

# The cache key depends on deps/ and on the workflows under .github/.
local_key_inputs() { echo "$(git rev-parse "$1:.github") $(git rev-parse "$1:deps")"; }
remote_key_inputs() {
  gh api "repos/$REPO/git/trees/$1" < /dev/null \
    --jq '[.tree[] | select(.path == ".github" or .path == "deps") | {key: .path, value: .sha}] | from_entries | "\(.[".github"]) \(.deps)"'
}

# Prints the id of a push build of the base branch that has not finished, is not
# one of the ids in $1, and has KEY_INPUTS.
matching_base_build() {
  local status runs id sha
  runs=$(for status in in_progress queued pending waiting requested; do
    gh api -X GET "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/$workflow/runs" \
      -f branch="$BASE_REF" -f event=push -f status="$status" -f per_page=10 < /dev/null \
      | jq -r '.workflow_runs[] | "\(.id) \(.head_sha)"'
  done)
  while read -r id sha; do
    [ -n "$id" ] || continue
    [[ " ${1:-} " == *" $id "* ]] && continue
    if [ "$(remote_key_inputs "$sha")" = "$KEY_INPUTS" ]; then
      echo "$id"
      return
    fi
  done <<< "$runs"
}

check() {
  KEY_INPUTS=$(local_key_inputs HEAD)
  out "key-inputs=$KEY_INPUTS"
  if [ "$KEY_INPUTS" != "$(local_key_inputs HEAD^1)" ]; then
    echo "This pull request changes deps/ or .github/, so it builds its own deps."
    return
  fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Brings a dependency build folder (deps/build/<arch>) up to date with the
# deps/ recipe of the checkout you run it from, before you build the app
# against that folder:
#
#   scripts/deps_current.sh <deps build folder>
#
# The recipe's fingerprint is the git tree of deps/ (`git rev-parse HEAD:deps`),
# the same one OrcaSlicer's CI keys its deps cache on (scripts/ci_deps_cache.sh).
# After each successful build this script saves it in the folder as
# jusprin-deps-recipe.txt. When the saved fingerprint differs from this
# checkout's, or none is saved yet, it builds the folder's `deps` target, which
# rebuilds only the libraries whose recipe changed, then saves the new one.
#
# The folder builds from the deps/ it was configured with (its CMakeCache's
# CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY), often another checkout. If that checkout's recipe is
# not this checkout's, building cannot help, and the script says so and fails.
# It also fails on uncommitted changes to either deps/, which no fingerprint
# describes.
set -euo pipefail

folder=${1:?usage: scripts/deps_current.sh <deps build folder>}
folder=$(cd "$folder" && pwd)
cache="$folder/CMakeCache.txt"
[ -f "$cache" ] || { echo "deps_current: $folder has no CMakeCache.txt; configure it first (build_release_macos.sh -d)." >&2; exit 1; }

here=$(git -C "$(dirname "$0")" rev-parse --show-toplevel)
source_deps=$(sed -n 's/^CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY:INTERNAL=//p' "$cache")
source_repo=$(git -C "$source_deps" rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cmake_bin=$(sed -n 's/^CMAKE_COMMAND:INTERNAL=//p' "$cache")

for repo in "$here" "$source_repo"; do
    if ! git -C "$repo" diff --quiet HEAD -- deps; then
        echo "deps_current: $repo has uncommitted changes under deps/; commit or drop them first." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
done

want=$(git -C "$here" rev-parse HEAD:deps)
source_recipe=$(git -C "$source_repo" rev-parse HEAD:deps)
if [ "$want" != "$source_recipe" ]; then
    echo "deps_current: $folder builds from $source_repo, whose deps/ recipe ($source_recipe) is not this checkout's ($want)." >&2
    echo "deps_current: bring that checkout to this recipe, or build a deps folder of your own." >&2
    exit 1
fi

record="$folder/jusprin-deps-recipe.txt"
have=$(cat "$record" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ "$have" = "$want" ]; then
    echo "deps_current: $folder is up to date with deps/ $want."
    exit 0
fi

echo "deps_current: $folder is out of date (built from ${have:-an unrecorded recipe}, now $want); building its deps target."
if pgrep -f "$folder" >/dev/null; then
    echo "deps_current: something is already building in $folder; wait for it, then run this again." >&2
    exit 1
fi
config=$(sed -n 's/^CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE:STRING=//p' "$cache")
"$cmake_bin" --build "$folder" --config "${config:-Release}" --target deps -- -j4
echo "$want" > "$record"
echo "deps_current: $folder is now up to date with deps/ $want."

content.text:
I've written the script that keeps the shared dependency build folder current, and changed the release skill to use it. Both are in one local commit. Nothing is pushed or on `jusprin-dev` yet. The real rebuild of the main checkout's dependency folder, and its timing, wait until 2.0.1 lands.

**How the script works.** You run `scripts/deps_current.sh <dependency build folder>`, for example the main checkout's `deps/build/arm64`. It takes a fingerprint of the `deps/` recipe from git, the same one OrcaSlicer's CI uses for its dependency cache, and compares it with the fingerprint saved in that folder after its last build. If they differ, or none is saved yet, it rebuilds the folder's dependencies with 4 jobs and saves the new fingerprint. It stops with a message, without building, in these cases:
- The checkout the folder was set up from has a different `deps/` recipe than yours. Rebuilding wouldn't help then.
- Either checkout has uncommitted changes under `deps/`.
- Another run is already building that folder.

**What I tested.** I used fake folders where cmake was replaced by a command that does nothing, then by one that always fails. Every case behaved as intended:
- A folder with no saved fingerprint gets built and then has one.
- A second run says the folder is up to date.
- A folder set up from the OrcaSlicer checkout is refused because its recipe differs.
- A held lock is refused.
- A failed build keeps the old fingerprint and frees the lock.

shellcheck reports nothing. The script hasn't run a real dependency build yet.

**What changed in the commit:**
- **Build step:** the skill now runs the script first. The old workaround is gone: it built Sentry alone into a scratch folder, and the build then needed an extra `-Dsentry_DIR` flag.
- **Server check:** the skill now says any 4xx answer except 404 means the address exists on the server.
- **AGENTS.md:** one line under "Building on a shared machine" tells other agents to run the script before building against a dependency folder built earlier.

**Still open:**

Kenneth asked for this step (his words: "once the new version is released, open the old version to see if it automatically prompts for upgrade"). Add it to your after-publish steps. Do it only once he has published 2.0.1, because the update check reads only published releases. Don't start it before that.

How to run it: start the installed 2.0.0 app without touching anything. Here is what the code suggests, which this test should confirm or disprove. The background check runs about 10 s after startup, then once an hour, but it asks the server at most once every 24 h (key `jusprin_update_last_attempt` in the app's conf). It does nothing when Preferences › Updates "check automatically" is off or stealth mode is on. A version it finds appears only in Preferences › Updates; I found no popup, banner or notice anywhere else. So before you start 2.0.0, make sure its last attempt is more than a day old, or use a fresh datadir. Wait at least a minute. Record what appears on its own, with a screenshot. Then open Preferences › Updates and check that it offers 2.0.1. Report both results to Kenneth plainly, including "nothing appeared on its own" if that is what happens.

# Python depends on OpenSSL and ZLIB
if(TARGET dep_OpenSSL)
    add_dependencies(dep_python3 dep_OpenSSL)
endif()
if(TARGET dep_ZLIB)
    add_dependencies(dep_python3 dep_ZLIB)
endif()

if (NOT WIN32)
    # _ssl and _hashlib embed the static OpenSSL built in deps/ (Windows uses
    # CPython's prebuilt OpenSSL instead). Their Makefile rules depend only on
    # their own sources, not on the OpenSSL archives, so a rebuilt OpenSSL does
    # not make them relink and they keep the previous one. On an incremental tree,
    # drop the built modules and relink them against the current OpenSSL; a
    # fresh build is left alone (its PGO target builds them). "make" alone is a
    # no-op once PGO has run, so sharedmods is invoked explicitly.
    ExternalProject_Get_Property(dep_python3 SOURCE_DIR)
    file(GLOB _python_ssl_modules
        "${SOURCE_DIR}/Modules/_ssl*.so"
        "${SOURCE_DIR}/Modules/_hashlib*.so")
    if (_python_ssl_modules)
        ExternalProject_Add_Step(dep_python3 relink_ssl_extensions
            DEPENDEES configure
            DEPENDERS build
            COMMAND sh -c "rm -f '${SOURCE_DIR}'/Modules/_ssl*.so '${SOURCE_DIR}'/Modules/_hashlib*.so && make -j${NPROC} sharedmods"
            WORKING_DIRECTORY "${SOURCE_DIR}"
            COMMENT "CPython: relinking _ssl/_hashlib against the current OpenSSL"
            DEPENDS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_FILE}"
                    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/../OpenSSL/OpenSSL.cmake"
        )
    endif ()
endif ()

   - **Building `deps`:** building the `deps` target of a Unix-Makefiles ExternalProject tree rebuilds only the libraries whose recipe changed.
   - **Python relink step:** an upstream step (`deps/python3/python3.cmake`, commit 8585eae816) relinks CPython's `_ssl`/`_hashlib` on incremental trees. CPython's Makefile calls the toolchain's cc without an SDK, so the link needs SDKROOT. CI never hits this because it builds fresh. `build_release_macos.sh -d` on a folder built before would also fail.
   - **App update check (UpdateCheck.cpp, UpdateRecord.cpp):**
     - The first check runs 10 s after start, then hourly.
     - It asks the server at most once per 24 h (key `jusprin_update_last_attempt`).
     - It is skipped when automatic checking is off or stealth mode is on.
     - The result shows only in Preferences › Updates. I found no popup elsewhere; this is inferred from the code and not yet tested.

     #!/usr/bin/env bash
     # (header comment: usage scripts/deps_current.sh <deps build folder>; fingerprint = git tree of deps/; saved as jusprin-deps-recipe.txt; fails if the folder's source checkout recipe differs or deps/ has uncommitted changes)
     set -euo pipefail
     folder=${1:?usage: scripts/deps_current.sh <deps build folder>}
     folder=$(cd "$folder" && pwd)
     cache="$folder/CMakeCache.txt"
     [ -f "$cache" ] || { echo "deps_current: $folder has no CMakeCache.txt; configure it first (build_release_macos.sh -d)." >&2; exit 1; }
     here=$(git -C "$(dirname "$0")" rev-parse --show-toplevel)
     source_deps=$(sed -n 's/^CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY:INTERNAL=//p' "$cache")
     source_repo=$(git -C "$source_deps" rev-parse --show-toplevel)
     cmake_bin=$(sed -n 's/^CMAKE_COMMAND:INTERNAL=//p' "$cache")
     for repo in "$here" "$source_repo"; do  # fail on uncommitted deps/ changes
         if ! git -C "$repo" diff --quiet HEAD -- deps; then ...; exit 1; fi

I've worked out the permanent design, but I've stopped before building it. Keeping your Mac as a build machine for a public repository lets some strangers' pull requests run code on it.

**The design (proposed, not built).** On your Mac, the Mac build jobs would skip GitHub's cache and keep the prebuilt libraries in a folder outside the job's working folder, such as `~/jusprin-ci/deps/<arch>/<recipe fingerprint>`. The fingerprint is the same one the cache key uses today, so the libraries are rebuilt only when the recipe under `deps/` changes. A new recipe gets a fresh full build, about an hour per architecture, and older folders get pruned. Everything else stays the same as today: GitHub's Macs, Linux and Windows still use the cache. The runner moves out of `/private/tmp` into a permanent folder and runs as a service.

**The security problem.** I checked these facts:

- The repository is public.
- The organization is on GitHub's free plan.
- Pull requests from forks need approval before their workflows run only for first-time contributors. That setting is `first_time_contributors`.

So someone who has had one pull request merged can open another that edits a workflow to say "run on self-hosted". It would run on your Mac with no approval, with access to your files and your logged-in sessions. GitHub's own documentation warns against self-hosted runners on public repositories for this reason.

My unverified understanding is that GitHub's setting to limit a runner to certain workflows isn't available on the free plan. I can't check that myself: my GitHub token isn't allowed to read the organization's runner settings.

**Decision needed:** how should your Mac be protected?

- **Require approval for every outside contributor's pull request (my pick).** This changes the repository's setting from "first-time contributors" to "all outside contributors". Workflows on a stranger's pull request then run only after someone with write access clicks approve. The cost is that every outside pull request waits for a click before its checks run. The risk left is that whoever approves must glance at whether the pull request touches `.github/workflows/`. Only you can change this setting, under Settings › Actions › General.
- **Use a separate Mac for builds instead of your own.** For example, a Mac mini that holds nothing but the signing certificate, or a rented cloud Mac. Even if a pull request got through, it would reach nothing of yours. It costs money and setup time, and I haven't priced it.

Which do you want? Until this is settled, I'm leaving everything as it is. 2.0.1 still has no Mac files, and nothing has been published.
